title: Rewriting the billing module across five services in one PR
hidden_flaw: Big-bang replacement without seams: no way to ship incrementally, compare old vs new outputs, or roll back one part; a months-long branch diverges from main; proration and tax edge cases have no characterisation tests. Should introduce a seam (interface/anti-corruption layer), add characterisation/golden tests on current behaviour, then strangle module by module with shadow mode / parallel run comparing invoices.
notes: Fundamental flaw: big-bang multi-module rewrite without seams or behavioural safety net.

input.objective: Replace the legacy billing calculation code (invoices, proration, tax) with a clean domain model so new pricing plans can be added in days instead of weeks.
constraints: Billing errors directly cost money and trust; finance reconciles invoices monthly.
Team of 3 engineers; other feature work continues on main in parallel.
Must support existing plans exactly (including grandfathered ones).
input.context: Billing logic is spread across 5 services (subscriptions, invoicing, tax, payments, notifications) in a TypeScript monorepo, ~14k LOC, with shared mutable 'BillingContext' objects passed around. Test coverage of billing code is ~22%, mostly happy paths. There are 37 pricing plans, 11 grandfathered. Proration rules have known undocumented quirks that customers rely on.
input.proposed_solution: Create a long-lived branch `billing-v2` and rewrite all billing logic in a new `packages/billing-core` package with a clean domain model (Plan, Subscription, Invoice, ProrationPolicy). Update all 5 services to call billing-core, delete the old code, and merge everything in one PR when finished (~3 months). Write unit tests for the new domain model as we go. A single cut-over avoids maintaining two implementations at once.
